First, let $u=x+12.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

We can now rewrite the integral in terms of $u,$ solve it, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{x+12}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+12|+C\end{aligned}
$$
